key_takeaways: Two foreigners who do not live in France cannot marry at a French mairie, except in a commune of a French overseas collectivity or New Caledonia; the Australian Embassy in France says at least one of you must be a French citizen or a legal resident of France.
The commune must be where one of you has your home (domicile), or where one of you or a parent of one of you has lived for at least one month of continuous living by the date the banns are published.

Australians get the certificat de coutume in French from the Australian Embassy in Paris (AUD 181 per certificate, 2026 fee, valid 90 days) or have a DFAT Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) translated by a sworn translator.
A religious wedding in France may not take place before the civil marriage at the mairie, while a symbolic celebration has no legal effect and can be held at the venue you choose.

If neither of you qualifies, you can marry legally in Australia by giving a Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM) to an authorised celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months ahead, then celebrate in France.

faq.q: Can foreigners legally get married in France?
faq.a: Yes, if at least one of you is a French citizen or a legal resident of France, says the Australian Embassy in France, and you marry at the mairie of a commune that meets the residence rule below.

faq.q: Can two Australians get married in France without living there?
faq.a: Not at a mairie in France, apart from the overseas collectivities and New Caledonia. The alternative is a legal ceremony in Australia, then your celebration in France.

faq.q: How long do you need to live in France to get married?
faq.a: The commune must be where one of you has your home (domicile), or where one of you or a parent of one of you has lived for at least one month of continuous living by the date the banns are published. Proof must be in that person's name, and at least one of you must be French or a legal resident of France.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get married in France?
faq.a: The official Australian costs are AUD 181 per certificat de coutume or CNI and AUD 105 per apostille (2026 fees, rising with CPI each 1 January). Ask sworn translators and interpreters for a quote. Venue and guest costs depend on your plans; start with our France destination page.

faq.q: Is a French marriage legally recognised in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes, if it was valid in France and would have been valid under Australian law, says Smartraveller. You cannot register it in Australia; the French certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, though it may not be enough for a name change.

faq.q: Can we have a church wedding in France without a civil ceremony?
faq.a: No. Service-public says it is forbidden to celebrate a religious marriage before the civil marriage, so the mairie comes first. If you married legally in Australia, ask the officiant and the mairie early how that rule applies to you.
